Simulate data for a false-positive occupancy model

Source: R/simulate_fp.R
simulate_fp.Rd

Generates one dataset from known parameters under the multiple-methods design: an automated method that returns true detections and false positives at every site, and a verified method, free of false positives, at a random subset of sites. The false-positive rate can be homogeneous, vary at random among sites (unstructured), or track a latent gradient correlated with the occupancy covariate (structured confusion, as when a soundalike species becomes commoner along the same gradient as the target).

Usage

simulate_fp(
  nsite = 300,
  nocc = 20,
  psi = 0.5,
  b1 = -0.8,
  p11 = 0.6,
  p10 = 0.05,
  sigma_p10 = 0,
  p10_conc = NULL,
  conf_effect = 0,
  conf_cor = 0,
  r11 = 0.6,
  frac_verified = 0.3,
  nver = 3,
  a_bio = 0,
  a_aci = 0,
  sd_recorder = 0,
  nrec = 5,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

nsite

Number of sites.

nocc

Number of automated occasions per site.

psi

Occupancy probability at the mean of the covariate.

b1

Occupancy slope on the standardized covariate x.

p11

True-detection probability of the automated method at the mean of the detection covariates.

p10

False-positive probability of the automated method (its base value; the realized mean over sites is returned as truth$p10_marginal).

sigma_p10

Among-site standard deviation of the logit of the false-positive rate (unstructured, logit-normal heterogeneity). 0 for none.

p10_conc

Optional concentration of a Beta distribution for the site-level false-positive rate, with mean p10 (unstructured, aggregated heterogeneity; small values push rates towards 0 or 1). Overrides sigma_p10.

conf_effect

Slope of the logit of the false-positive rate on the confusing gradient w (structured confusion). 0 for none.

conf_cor

Correlation between w and the occupancy covariate x.

r11

Detection probability of the verified method.

frac_verified

Probability that a site is verified.

nver

Number of verified occasions per verified site.

a_bio, a_aci

Effects of two standardized observation covariates (bio, aci) on true detection. 0 by default.

sd_recorder

Standard deviation of a recorder random intercept on true detection. 0 by default.

nrec

Number of recorders.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A list of class fp_sim with elements data (an fp_data object whose sites table holds x and w, and whose auto table holds bio, aci, and recorder) and truth (the generating values, the realized mean false-positive rate p10_marginal, the realized correlation between w and x, and the latent states z).

Details

The occupancy covariate x is standardized, so b1 is the true slope exactly. The confusing gradient is \(w = \rho x + \sqrt{1 - \rho^2} \epsilon\), with \(\epsilon\) standard normal, so it has unit variance and correlation \(\rho\) with x. In practice w is not observed; it is returned in sites so that a model given the true structure can serve as a positive control. The function draws random numbers in the same order as simulate_fp() of the fpcalib research compendium (v0.1.0), with nsite, nocc, frac_verified, nver, sd_recorder, and nrec corresponding to its nsite, K, verified_coverage, n_verified, sig_u, and nobser.

See also

fp_occu(), fp_calibrate()

Examples

# homogeneous false positives
s0 <- simulate_fp(nsite = 100, nocc = 10, seed = 1)
s0
#> <fp_sim> homogeneous false positives
#>   truth: psi = 0.50, b1 = -0.80, p11 = 0.60, p10 = 0.050 (realized mean 0.050), r11 = 0.60
#>   realized occupancy: 0.49
#> <fp_data>
#>   sites:                  100
#>   automated occasions:    1000 (naive occupancy 0.70)
#>   verified sites:         32 (96 occasions, 12 with a confirmed detection)
#>   recorders:              5
#>   site covariates:        x, w 
#>   observation covariates: bio, aci 

# structured confusion
s1 <- simulate_fp(nsite = 100, nocc = 10, conf_effect = 1.5,
                  conf_cor = 0.7, seed = 1)
s1$truth$p10_marginal
#> [1] 0.1081844
